blocks.heading: Set it up
lines: Draw the network: towns as dots, roads or pipes as lines, the distance, time, cost or flow written on each line.
Mark one-way links with arrows before you read the questions.

blocks.heading: Shortest routes
lines: Start from the origin and write the least distance to each town you reach.
When a longer-looking route turns out cheaper, cross out the old figure and write the new one.
Most CAT networks have under 10 towns, so checking the few short routes by hand is quick.
A closed road: rerun the labels from the town just before it.

blocks.heading: Flows
lines: At a junction that keeps nothing, what comes in equals what goes out. Write one equation for each junction.
Start at a town or junction with only one unknown pipe and work outward.

blocks.heading: Counting routes
lines: List routes in a fixed order, by the first road taken, so none is counted twice.
"No town visited twice" rules out loops. "Exactly three roads" and "at most three" are different counts.

blocks.heading: Traps
lines: One-way links, and a toll charged per entry rather than per trip.
A question that changes the network (a road closed, a pipe capped) applies only to that question unless it says otherwise.
